speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: They are contradictions in terms as the use of violence automatically negates the notion of family or intimacy or relationship.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: The two concepts cannot and should not coexist in the same space.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Families and intimate relationships are, by definition, places of love, safety and comfort, not places where any member lives in fear of being controlled, humiliated, hurt, raped or killed.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Despite my misgivings, throughout my speech, I will use the term "intimate partner violence" (IPV) as this term tends to emphasise the relational nature of the violence rather than where the violence occurs.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: I am also the president of Persatuan Pemudi Islam Singapura (PPIS), a non-profit organisation focused on women empowerment.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: The Singapore Council of Women’s Organisations who run Star Shelter, a residential service for women who have experienced family violence, reports that it takes women living with violence an average of between four and seven years before they seek help.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Between 2018 and 2020, the number of enquiries related to family violence received by Family Service Centres or Protection Specialist Centres increased by 57% over the two years.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: The number of new cases of family violence taken up by Family Service Centres or Protection Specialist Centres increased by 125% over the five years.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: On a global level, in 2014, United Nations Secretary-General Ban Ki-moon described violence against women and girls as "A global pandemic that destroys lives, fractures communities and holds back development" and "the most extreme example of the political, financial, social and economic oppression of women and girls worldwide." Mr Speaker, data published in 2022 by Lancet indicates that globally, about 27% of women aged between 15 and 49 years who have ever been in a relationship have experienced physical and/or sexual intimate partner violence, with 13% experiencing it in the year before they were surveyed.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: The same data shows that this violence starts early, with 24% of girls aged 15 to 19 years and 26% of young women aged 19 to 24 years who have ever been in a relationship having experienced physical and/or sexual intimate partner violence.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: This figure is almost 30 times higher than the 5,000-plus reports on family violence made to Police in 2020.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: In doing so, we should consider definitions and the scope of IPV, trends across age, ethnicity, faith and gender, as well as emerging trends such as online violence, coercive control and violence where children are the perpetrators.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Importantly, we also need to have age and culturally sensitive discussions with women and girls as well as men and boys about gender roles and the causes and use of IPV.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: This is in no way intended to discount or diminish the stories of the many men who live with or have lived with IPV, but to honour the countless girls and women I have met and known personally and professionally throughout my life whose lives have been altered profoundly because of violence used by men.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: It is, however, important that men who are victims of IPV feel empowered to break their silence, are believed when they come forward and receive timely, effective and gender-sensitive support.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: I met my friend when we were both 12 years old and we grew up together.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: She was a sister to me and a daughter to my parents, and I watched with sadness as her life trajectory was hampered because of violence.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: The impact of IPV on my friend was not just cuts and bruises, but long-term emotional vulnerability, ongoing health issues, financial hardship, accommodation insecurity, difficulty in forming trusting relationships and children who grew up with a destructive male role model rather than a father.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Three weeks before her death, I was talking with her about a speech I was going to make in Parliament about gender inequality and my hope that my speech might make a difference.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: The day of my speech, my friend sent me a text message which I will read, "You will be great.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Just think of all the oppressed women out there and that they need a voice.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Speak from the heart, and with the strength you have so bravely built in yourself over the years." So, this is for you, my beautiful friend, and for all the other women, like my friend, whose lives are now not how they should be.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: We are talking about real women with real lives and with real pain, sorrow, disadvantage and trauma.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: IPV can so easily be dismissed as simply "he hit her", but, Mr Speaker, it is so much more.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: It is a betrayal of a women's trust, confidence, safety and a sense of self – and it can stay with her forever.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: As also noted by Dr Bath, "Children see.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: More than we think." I am not raising this issue to criticise the choice made by some women with children to remain living with IPV, as many simply have no alternative, but to highlight that we as a system must do far more to protect children.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Where violence exists, children should never be a second thought.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: The system needs to be far faster and better at removing the abuser and ensuring that women and their children are physically and emotionally safe, and have immediate access to dignified and secure accommodation, free legal advice, income support when needed and trauma informed care.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Girls exposed to IPV are more likely to tolerate or even seek out such behaviour in their own future relationships.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Boys exposed to IPV are more likely to see violence against women as the norm and to use violence in their own future relationships.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: By failing to protect children from exposure to IPV, we are not only harming children, we are also perpetuating the inter-generational cycle of accepting and using violence in relationships.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: While some may argue that elder abuse is not technically IPV, it is still a form of violence that occurs within a domestic environment and which usually involves family members or those living within the family home as perpetrators.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: For this reason, and because many elderly people are inherently vulnerable, I am including elder abuse in my comments today.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Like with other forms of in-home violence, information about elder abuse in Singapore is slim.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: As with the data on general rates of IPV, these figures may not capture the full extent of elder abuse in Singapore as it is likely that many incidents go unreported.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: While the preference for home-based care is influenced by cultural values, and the unavailability and expense of professional residential care, home-based care carries with it significant risks, including: inadequate carer qualifications or training; social isolation and a lack of external oversight; inadequate or inaccessible home infrastructure; cramped or undignified living conditions and caregiver stress and fatigue.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: While this might be difficult, given the sheer number of older people being cared for at home and cultural barriers about accepting such a service, current practice remains inherently risky.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: This is on top of previously existing initiatives, some of which have been in place for decades.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: It can be tough work and can take its toll; particularly when it sometimes feels as if the broader system is unaware or indifferent to the issue.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: I know what it is like to work in a sector that is specialised, frequently under-resourced and for the most part, invisible.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: To all of you out there in IPV land, you are not invisible to me, nor to many of my colleagues in Government, academia and the community sector; and, once again, I thank you for everything you do.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: And, require organisations to provide Domestic Violence Awareness Training to all managers and staff, and have policies to guide organisational response to employees who may be affected by IPV.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Every one of us has a right and an inherent need to feel and be safe, always and everywhere, and not just by chance or life circumstances, but by assurance.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: In 2024, MSF released our Domestic Violence Trends Report.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: No one should experience violence, especially at the hands of a person whom they should love and trust.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Our work to prevent and eradicate domestic violence is a continuous, intensive piece of work that we engage in together with our community and social service partners.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Every day, we are thinking about how to better protect survivors and to hold perpetrators to account.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Kindly allow me to share the framework we have in place in Singapore to tackle domestic violence.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We have five key pieces of legislation in place to address domestic violence.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Rehabilitative orders can be issued with a Personal Protection Order.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This includes the counselling order, which can be mandated by the Courts and the counselling conducted by the social service agencies.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This reflects the Ministry's approach to domestic violence, which emphasises the repairing of harm and the mending of relationships, and is aligned with the spirit of Restorative Justice.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: In line with the enhanced punishments under the Penal Code for offences against vulnerable persons and intimate partners, the penalties for offences under the Protection from Harassment Act (POHA) against vulnerable persons and intimate partners was doubled in 2019.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Third, the POHA Protection Orders regime was strengthened by establishing a dedicated Protection from Harassment Court.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Fourth, for those who cannot protect themselves from abuse because of a mental or physical infirmity, disability or incapacity, we have the Vulnerable Adults Act introduced in 2018.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Fifth, underwriting all this is the Criminal Procedure Code, which is the main piece of legislation that provides the powers and procedures for enforcing our criminal laws to hold perpetrators to account.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Complementing the legal framework, we have upstream and downstream efforts to tackle domestic violence.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: I appreciate the Member's call for the community to be engaged.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: And indeed, preventing and addressing violence is a whole of society effort.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Examples of MSF's upstream efforts include: partnering Institutes of Higher Learning to drive awareness on respectful relationships amongst youths; partnering ethnic organisations and community agencies on domestic violence topics to foster community awareness; and running domestic violence awareness training workshops to equip the community with the knowledge to spot and safely intervene when they see potential cases of domestic violence in the community.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We have also invested in public education to increase awareness of abuse through our "Break The Silence" campaign.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We note the Member's feedback that home-based care for the elderly may increase the risk of social isolation or abuse due to caregiver stress, and her suggestion for home visitation services.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Our Silver Generation Office currently reaches out to those aged 60 and above to identify needs and refer them to relevant support or services, such as Active Ageing Centres for befriending and buddying service.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Where violence has taken place, 24-hour services are available to facilitate reporting and for survivors to receive immediate help: the National Anti-Violence and Sexual Harassment Helpline was enhanced in 2022 to include online reporting.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The Domestic Violence Emergency Response Team (DVERT) was introduced in 2023, where social service professionals respond jointly with the Police in high-risk cases with immediate safety concerns.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The Member suggested on-site issuance of Personal Protection Orders against perpetrators.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The Emergency Order may also include a Domestic Exclusion Order, a Stay Away Order or a No Contact Order imposed on the perpetrator.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: A breach of any of these orders is an arrestable offence.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Our social service agencies are our key partners in the efforts to tackle domestic violence, and I would like to commend our Family Service Centres, Protection Specialist Centres and the Integrated Service for Individual and Family Protection Specialist Centre, for partnering us on this journey.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The Member highlighted the importance of other elements of support, such as immediate financial support and expediting purchase or rental of HDB property for survivors.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Their immediate need is to be referred to crisis shelters, who will work with survivors to address their safety concerns and to assist them in subsequently securing stable housing arrangements.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: I have also written letters to the Ministry of National Development before, to facilitate rental housing for these survivors, so I know that it can be done.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: And those who require urgent financial assistance may also tap on Interim Assistance, which provides immediate one-off financial assistance to individuals and families requiring urgent and temporary financial relief.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Those who need longer term support for their basic needs can also be referred to the Social Service Offices for ComCare assistance.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: These efforts aim to empower survivors to stay safe and work towards financial independence, in line with what the Member has suggested.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: There is also support for perpetrators who cannot remain in their homes due to statutory orders.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: If they are unable to find alternate accommodation, they can seek assistance from transitional shelters.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: And over the years, the training of social workers to deliver support and services to the survivors has been enhanced.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The Member has also highlighted the importance of a nationwide response and framework to end domestic violence.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: As she has shared, this is in the form of the Taskforce on Family Violence, which I co-chaired with Minister of State for Home Affairs Assoc Prof Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: And within the MSF, we also have specialised Protective Service units, which are part of a larger Rehabilitation and Protection Group in the MSF.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The employers' greatest contribution is to support survivors to rebuild their lives, by giving them the opportunity of a job and to thrive in the workplace.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Beyond that, I am a bit mindful that we should not make employers do things which the Government or the community is better equipped to do.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: To conclude, I would like to reiterate that the Government takes a strong stance against violence.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: But we cannot do this alone because of the hidden nature of domestic violence.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Addressing domestic violence requires a whole-of-society approach, and I thank the Member for her speech, which not only highlights this important issue, but also emphasises how this is a shared responsibility.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Everyone has a part to play in building a society where families are strong and everyone feels safe.
